summary: Repair A0046 review-002 finding: align docs/spec/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md §2.2 line 237-238 with the corrected A0046 ownership split recorded in docs/spec/security/THREAT_MODEL.md T-21 and the §4 severity matrix. The sentence that previously read 'T111 performs the approved-consumer cutover' now reads 'T111 owns the approved T101/T102/T106 consumer compatibility view, and T113 owns the supported CLI composition and old-path cutover', matching the T-21 wording and every T111/T113 reference in docs/spec/. No other §2.2 text changed, no gate was weakened, and the candidate remains byte-identical on every protected surface.
rationale: Independent review-002 returned FAIL because the previous repair correctly updated THREAT_MODEL.md T-17/T-21/T-22 controls, owner rows, evidence rows and the §4 severity matrix to attribute the approved-consumer compatibility view to T111 and the supported CLI composition and old-path cutover to T113, but left the §2.2 ARCHITECTURE.md sentence at lines 237-238 still saying 'T111 performs the approved-consumer cutover'. That sentence names T111 as the actor performing the cutover, which contradicts both the new T-21 wording and the rest of the §2.2 prose (T109 row, T111/T113 module rows, and the 'T113 is the planned cutover' paragraph). This repair rewrites only that one sentence, using the exact same ownership language as THREAT_MODEL.md T-21 (line 472-474). The intent/specification/contracts/dependencies/implementation/data/operations/security/verification impact summary mirrors the previous candidate, with the specification dimension updated to reflect that the architecture/Spec split is now internally consistent. The seven impact-gated open contracts (T084, T087, T088, T096, T103, T110, T111) recorded by review-001 remain open because they live in Planner-owned task contracts that a future CONTRACT amendment must revise before activation; this documentation repair does not resolve any of them.

impact_assessment.intent: No product intent or V1 boundary change. This repair removes a residual internal contradiction in the architecture Spec created by the previous candidate, identical in scope to the previous candidate.
impact_assessment.specification: ARCHITECTURE.md §2.2 line 237-238 now attributes the approved T101/T102/T106 consumer compatibility view to T111 and the supported CLI composition and old-path cutover to T113, matching THREAT_MODEL.md T-21 (line 472-474) and the §4 severity matrix (lines 551, 555, 556). Every other T111/T113 reference in docs/spec/ already agreed; the docs/spec/* surface is now internally consistent. No other §2.2 text changed; the Spec revision v1-2026-09-25-contract-first-component-boundaries and intent_revision are unchanged.
impact_assessment.contracts: No contract file rewritten. Added only T113 in the previous candidate; the seven impact-gated open contracts (T084, T087, T088, T096, T103, T110, T111) remain open and require a reviewed CONTRACT amendment before activation.
impact_assessment.dependencies: Existing dependency records remain unchanged. T113 still depends on the approved replay, feature, engine, dataset and T112 authorities; T087/T103 impacts still require a later reviewed dependency amendment to T113.
impact_assessment.implementation: No application code changes. The repair edits only documentation. Current CLI start/resume still use predecessor BacktestOrchestrator and default empty source; T113 will compose T100→T040/T041→T050→T061→T112 and close the CLI old-writer path.
impact_assessment.data: No persisted data format is changed by this planning amendment. T113 must preserve approved T112 and historical artifact bytes and keep predecessor records read-only.
impact_assessment.operations: CLI currently fails closed with its default empty event source; successful current publication stays unavailable until reviewed T113 cutover. No operational procedure changes.
impact_assessment.security: No signer, key, signing, broadcast, execution, risk, or promotion authority is added or weakened by the documentation repair. Existing security boundaries remain binding.
impact_assessment.verification: Author review: workflow configuration validation (python -m tools.workflow validate reports OK), documentation links/citations, import-graph consistency, plan structure, and diff checks remain required before review. Independent amendment review remains required; no implementation test suite is applicable because no code changed and the repair only rewrites documentation already bound to the same evidence.

Preserve the existing read-model behavior and other dependencies, and verify current versus legacy rendering. Do not rewrite approved evidence or historical artifacts; no data migration, operations change, or security-authority change is applicable.
